title: Recap Verse: Production Multi-LLM AI Platform
description: An AI video platform that turns comic and webtoon chapters into narrated recap videos. It routes three LLM providers by task and decides who is speaking with a deterministic five-stage resolver instead of trusting the model's answer.
keyResults: Built and run alone, with paying subscribers and 2,100+ automated tests that run in CI on every pull request
Routes Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT and Google Gemini by task, falling back to the next connected provider on provider errors and never on configuration errors
A deterministic five-stage cast resolver, with no model call, replaced trusting the model's own claims about identity and who is speaking
Writes are compare-and-set, so an edit a user makes during a slow model call is never overwritten
Bring-your-own-key provider credentials are encrypted at rest with AES-GCM, and uploads are checked by file signature, type allow-list and size
JWT authentication with per-user ownership scoping enforced on every route, not trusted at the gateway
Five self-run stress-test rounds found and fixed an open redirect, rate limits bypassed by a spoofed X-Forwarded-For header, a missing request-body cap and HTML served from the app origin

title: BreachScope: Live Threat Intelligence Map
description: A live threat-intelligence map built on public security feeds, with provenance and location accuracy on every record.
keyResults: Load tested locally at 20,000 requests and 200 concurrent with zero errors and zero data races
Pulls C2 servers, malware hosts, scanners, exploited CVEs and breaches from ThreatFox, URLhaus, Feodo Tracker, SANS DShield, CISA KEV and Have I Been Pwned
The API serialises and compresses its snapshot once per refresh (1.4 MB to 175 KB) and the CDN serves it, so a spike in visitors is never a spike in requests to the feeds
Runs at $0 a month

title: R2Dock: Desktop Client for Cloudflare R2
description: An open-source desktop file manager for Cloudflare R2 with crash-safe multipart uploads, resumable downloads and keys held in the OS keychain. A Rust core does all I/O; the React interface never sees a secret or a local path. No backend, no telemetry.
keyResults: Stress-tested before release against a local S3-compatible server: 3,000 uploads and downloads totaling 1.3 GB, and 160,000 activity-log rows written from 32 threads
About 600 automated tests in Rust and Vitest, run in CI on Windows, macOS and Linux against an in-process S3-compatible server, so no CI run touches a real bucket
Multipart uploads run up to 4 parts in parallel with per-part checksums and an on-disk journal, so a pause, dropped connection or restart resumes where it stopped
Secrets go to macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or Linux Secret Service with a session-only fallback, never a plaintext file, and are never returned to the interface
Downloads treat object names as untrusted: they cannot leave the chosen folder, never follow symlinks and never overwrite without an explicit Replace
Nine releases from v0.1.1 to v0.5.2; v0.5.0 answered an outside audit of v0.4.1, and v0.5.1 patched RUSTSEC-2026-0382 and -0383

title: Spoonstill: Batch Photo-and-Narration Video Renderer
description: A batch renderer that turns a folder of stills and narration into one MP4, giving each image Ken Burns motion and cutting each scene on the length of its narration. A Rust workspace driving FFmpeg, with a CLI as the complete control surface and a thin Tauri desktop window on top.
keyResults: 4K caption rendering cut from 604 ms to 62 ms per cue by rewriting dilate as a sliding-window max and blur as a running sum, with byte-identical output
Validating a 200-scene project dropped from 11.82 s to 1.31 s (9x) after replacing a flat 20 ms poll with proportional backoff and concurrent probes
About 51,700 lines of Rust across 6 crates with 826 test functions and 39 shell exit gates that render real media through real FFmpeg
180 numbered entries in a decision log; architecture, no-shell-string and cited-decision rules are enforced by tests that fail the build
Every push runs 6 CI jobs, including cargo audit, full test suites on macOS and Windows, and both installers executed end to end
Measured the free voice service failing after 335 to 390 lines regardless of request rate, so renders wait out the limit instead of failing

title: OSPF Multi-Area Lab: 8 Routers, 5 Areas, OSPFv2 and OSPFv3
description: A Cisco Packet Tracer lab of eight OSPF routers in five areas, built and captured by script, and the basis for a 46-minute narrated course from the first Hello packet to multi-area design and troubleshooting.
keyResults: Area 2's link-state database dropped from 23 LSAs as a normal area to 18 as a stub and 3 as totally stubby
36 captured evidence steps, each applied by script with its raw show output saved
Summarizing area 1 as 10.1.0.0/16 replaced five routes with one, plus a Null0 discard route on the ABR
auto-cost reference-bandwidth 10000 separated 100 Mbps and 1 Gbps paths that tied at cost 1 by default
Seven injected faults diagnosed: hello timers, area ID, subnet mask, MTU, passive interface, duplicate router ID and network type
Documented where Packet Tracer departs from real IOS, including NSSA generating no Type 7 LSAs and an active virtual link producing bogus Type 4 LSAs and an external routing loop

title: DC1: Enterprise Data Center Network Lab
description: A redundant, segmented data center network in Cisco Packet Tracer 9 with dual cores, dual-homed racks, dual-ISP eBGP and a four-zone ASA firewall, tested by breaking it while traffic was running.
keyResults: Passed 12 of 12 acceptance flows, 8 required to work and 4 required to be blocked, both live and again after the saved file was reopened
Five failure drills under continuous ping: a rack uplink failure lost 0 of 200 packets, a core-to-core cable 1 of 240, and Core 1 powered off 35 of 250 while Core 2 took over every gateway
22 devices and 26 cables, with web, app and database tiers in separate VLANs and the database tier behind the firewall, unreachable from the web servers
ASA with four security zones (outside, DMZ, database, inside), static NAT for public web and DNS, and PAT for internal hosts
SSH-only management accepted only from the management VLAN, plus port security, BPDU guard and DHCP snooping on rack ports
Failover testing exposed the firewall's database cable as a single point of failure, so both firewall links moved onto the dual-homed rack switches

title: Hardened Static Page: CSP and Weight Budget Enforced in CI
description: A deliberately simple static page wrapped in a deny-by-default Content-Security-Policy, a page-weight budget and a CI pipeline that fails the build if either regresses.
keyResults: Cold page load cut from about 19.6 MB to 34 KB by replacing a 19,523,366-byte PNG with a 1,020-byte SVG, with Lighthouse 100/100/100/100 in CI
CSP of default-src 'none' with no unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval, made possible by self-hosting the font and dropping all 3 third-party hosts
CI injects an inline script into a copy of the page and fails if it runs, so the policy is tested for effect rather than for spelling
Five blocking CI jobs: lint, weight budget (critical path at most 150 KB), header checks, gitleaks across full history and Lighthouse
9 security headers, including 2-year HSTS with preload, COOP/COEP/CORP and a Permissions-Policy disabling 18 unused features
Supply chain: Actions pinned to commit SHAs and the gitleaks download verified by SHA-256

title: TrustKart: Full-Stack Store with a Virtual Wallet
description: An online electronics store with 1,260+ real products from 128 brands, where every visitor shops with $100,000 of virtual money. React on Vercel in front of a Spring Boot API and PostgreSQL on Render.
keyResults: Race-tested with 12 shoppers buying the last 3 units at once: exactly 3 sold, 9 rejected, stock never negative
Checkout is one database transaction that locks the wallet, re-prices every item server side and reserves stock in a fixed order, so orders never deadlock
One-time order keys make a double click or a retried request return the existing order instead of creating a second one
120+ server tests on real PostgreSQL and Redis via Testcontainers, plus Playwright shopping journeys on desktop and mobile in CI
Argon2id passwords, rotating refresh tokens in HttpOnly cookies, CSRF protection, a strict Content Security Policy and Bucket4j rate limiting

title: Hardening Linux Servers with iptables: Rate Limiting & NAT
description: A group term project for CYB623 that defends an Ubuntu host against attacks launched from a Kali VM using only iptables: a rate limiter for SSH brute force, limits on ICMP and SYN floods, and a DNAT redirect from port 80 to an Apache instance on 8080.
keyResults: SSH brute force: a source that makes 2 or more new connections in 120 seconds is dropped, using the recent module
ICMP and SYN floods are rate-limited with the limit module
Port 80 is redirected to Apache on 8080 with DNAT
The rules are applied by Bash scripts that CI checks with ShellCheck
Attacks were launched from the Kali VM with hydra and hping3

title: http-hardening-check: HTTP Hardening Auditor for Nmap
description: An Nmap script that audits HTTP security headers, cookies and CORS against a policy you control, scores each service from 0 to 100, and writes reports that can pass or fail a CI build.
keyResults: 321 tests: 94 Lua unit, 84 stress, 75 for the Python reporter, 36 for the GitHub Action and policies, and 32 integration tests against real Nmap
48 checks graded against three policy presets: baseline, strict and OWASP ASVS L1
Reports in JSON, CSV, Markdown, HTML and SARIF 2.1.0, the last validated against the official schema
A typo in a policy is an error, not a quietly weaker scan: unknown keys, unknown finding IDs and wrong types are rejected
The GitHub Action refuses targets that resolve to public addresses unless that is explicitly allowed

title: win-dev-sec-bootstrap: Windows Workstation Setup and Security Assessment
description: PowerShell tooling that sets up a Windows 10 or 11 workstation for development and security work, then checks how well it is protected: a read-only assessment of 27 Windows security controls with JSON and HTML evidence reports.
keyResults: Assesses 27 Windows security controls read-only and writes JSON and HTML evidence reports
Opt-in remediation for 13 controls with -WhatIf and -Confirm, the previous value backed up before each change and verified afterwards
Over 200 Pester tests and PSScriptAnalyzer, run in GitHub Actions on both PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1
Controls cite NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, MITRE ATT&CK or Microsoft Learn only where the relationship was checked against the source

title: Automating InfoSec: WinSecKit PowerShell Module
description: WinSecKit, a PowerShell module that detects attacker activity in Windows event logs, audits and hardens hosts, and turns the results into a shareable HTML report. It grew out of the CYB 631 coursework kept in the same repository.
keyResults: Run on a real Windows 11 machine and on CI runners: 10 bugs found and fixed
6 event-log detections, each mapped to a MITRE ATT&CK technique, with the rules kept as data rather than code
6 declarative host controls that can be audited, then remediated with -WhatIf support
103 Pester tests on both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, with PSScriptAnalyzer at zero suppressions
Found, purged and documented a leaked credential in the repository's own history, then added controls so it cannot recur

title: AWS EC2 Network Security Lab in Terraform
description: Terraform for a small EC2 environment with layered network controls: Security Groups, Network ACLs, IMDSv2, VPC Flow Logs, CloudWatch and SNS. CI checks it for misconfiguration before anything is deployed. It began as a 2025 console lab.
keyResults: No inbound management port: the instance is administered through Systems Manager Session Manager, so it has no SSH rule and no key pair
terraform test, TFLint and Checkov run on every push without AWS credentials: 10 plan-time assertions pass, and Checkov reports 121 passed, 0 failed and 7 documented skips
IMDSv2 is required, the EBS volume is encrypted, and VPC Flow Logs go to a KMS-encrypted CloudWatch Logs group
A mutation check confirms the tests fail when a deny rule is moved or IMDS is made optional

title: Cisco Rapid-PVST Campus Network Lab
description: A Cisco Packet Tracer campus lab: two distribution switches each root for one VLAN, two dual-homed access switches, and edge ports protected by BPDU Guard. The repository is archived.
keyResults: Per-VLAN roots: one distribution switch is root for VLAN 10 and the other for VLAN 20, so each access switch forwards on one uplink and blocks the other per VLAN
BPDU Guard err-disables the access port when a rogue switch is plugged in

title: x86-64 Assembly and Binary Hardening Lab
description: A beginner x86-64 assembly lab rebuilt as a binary-hardening project: it finds the security bugs in the original programs, fixes them, and checks in CI that they stay fixed. Includes asm-hexdump, a hexdump -C compatible tool written with raw syscalls.
keyResults: Found and fixed five bugs in the original programs: an executable stack, a misaligned printf call, an 8-byte load of a 4-byte value, a -no-pie workaround and exit status 0 on failed writes
An ELF hardening gate checks PIE, NX, RWX segments, text relocations and RELRO for each binary type, and is itself tested against known-bad binaries
57 tests cover exact stdout, stderr and exit status, with deterministic stress tests against independent references
asm-hexdump: about 300 lines of assembly with 4 KiB buffered I/O, correct across short reads
CI builds on native x86-64 with warnings as errors and requires byte-identical rebuilds

title: Regression Analysis of the College, Auto and Boston Datasets
description: A reproducible R analysis that compares linear, lasso and tree models on three ISLR datasets, with a held-out test set, a mean-only baseline, residual diagnostics, automated tests and CI. It began as a CS601C midterm at Pace University and was reworked with proper model evaluation.
keyResults: Fuel efficiency: log(mpg) on weight, year and origin reached a test RMSE of 3.04 mpg against 8.09 for a mean-only baseline (test R squared 0.86)
Every model is fitted on an 80% split, compared by 10-fold cross-validation on that split, and scored once on the remaining 20%
Data checks found two impossible values, percentages above 100, which are excluded in code while the raw CSV is left unchanged
The report is rendered and published by GitHub Actions on every push, with dependencies pinned by renv and unit tests in testthat

title: KokoroTTS: Offline Text-to-Speech Prototype
description: An early desktop wrapper around the Kokoro-82M ONNX voice model. It was replaced by SetupTTS, which now ships the Kokoro voices alongside online and built-in ones. The repository is archived.
keyResults: Superseded by SetupTTS and kept as a record of where that work started

title: TOC Extractor: Cross-Platform Web Novel Saver
description: A desktop app for Mac and Windows that reads a web novel's table of contents, lets you pick any chapters, and saves them as one clean TXT or PDF. Built in C# on .NET 10 with Avalonia, with the original Python tool kept as a tested reference implementation.
keyResults: Scale tested on 40 books at once across five sites, 2,000 chapters per run, with every saved chapter audited for gaps, order, duplicates and doubled paragraphs
Against version 2.2.1 on the same 40 books, average CPU fell from 272% to 142% and peak memory from 8.2 GB to 7.1 GB in the same time
Follows robots.txt (RFC 9309) and Crawl-delay; the C# and Python code decide robots.txt identically on a shared conformance corpus
Refuses redirects to private network addresses mid-chain, and never solves or works around a human-verification check
CI on Linux, Windows and macOS with warnings as errors; tagged releases build and self-test the Mac and Windows packages (v2.6.11, MIT)

title: WebAudioTV: Audiobook Streaming Platform
description: Streaming platform for audiobooks and long-form audio drama. Listeners play a three-level catalogue in a player that survives navigation and earn XP as they listen, publishers apply for a scoped workspace, and a PRO subscription unlocks downloads and early-access releases.
keyResults: 1,000+ commits, with 1,059 automated tests in 98 files, 100 versioned migrations and 25 Supabase edge functions (counted October 2026)
192 Row-Level Security policies over 40 tables, with roles kept in a separate user_roles table so a self-service profile edit can never grant admin

Audio never streams from a URL carrying a Supabase JWT: an HMAC token bound to (user_id, track_id, exp) is issued from an Authorization header, re-verified at the second hop, then SigV4-signed against Cloudflare R2
tracks.drive_file_url revoked at the column level from anon and authenticated, handed back only through a SECURITY DEFINER function that checks ownership in SQL
Non-R2 media fetches revalidate every redirect hop against an SSRF blocklist covering loopback, private ranges, link-local and cloud metadata addresses
A 48-check SQL access matrix runs as seven roles against the real migrations

title: SetupTTS: Cross-Platform Text-to-Speech Desktop App
description: Desktop app for macOS and Windows that turns text into MP3 with Microsoft's online neural voices (300+ in 70+ languages), offline Kokoro and Piper voices, or the computer's built-in voices. No API key. Built so a long export cannot silently lose a section.
keyResults: Assembly fails closed: before the MP3 is written the chunk ranges must tile the text exactly, every chunk must exist at its recorded size, and the audio length must be plausible for the text
25 releases up to v2.2.1, each packaged build launched with a self-test before it is published
Chunk limits are tuned per writing system. Han caps at 3,100 characters where Latin gets 10,500, because a CJK character is three UTF-8 bytes
Two no_audio failures stop retrying and subdivide the request instead of re-sending it; transient errors back off 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds
The offline HD voices run as ONNX on the same runtime Piper uses, so they add no dependencies and behave the same on macOS and Windows
Truncation detection: the streaming client can end quietly when the connection closes mid-response, so each section is checked against the service's own sentence timing before it is accepted

title: Dual-ISP Network Assessment & Subnet Remediation
description: Assessment of a home network running two independent routers on two separate internet plans with a NAS cabled to both, where both routers were configured on the same LAN subnet with the same gateway IP. Documents the discovery, the diagnosis and the remediation.
keyResults: Both routers were running 192.168.0.0/24 with the same gateway IP 192.168.0.1, leaving two physically separate LANs distinguishable only by router MAC address
Diagnosis required three separate scanning vantage points, because no single host could see both LANs: two machines behind Router A and one behind Router B
Mapped a dual-homed NAS present on both LANs and inventoried the services it exposed on each
Remediated by moving Router B and its NAS interface to a separate /24, which removed the duplicate subnet and gateway address
Deliverables include two inventory scanners (PowerShell and macOS shell), per-machine scan output, topology diagrams, an IEEE-style PDF report and a slide deck
Scope was limited to inventory and connectivity on an authorized private network. The tooling performs no exploits and makes no configuration changes

title: JEE Test Simulator: BYOK Exam Engine
description: Upload a JEE Main question paper and answer key as PDFs, have a vision-capable LLM of your choosing turn them into 75 structured questions, then sit the paper in a reproduction of the NTA exam portal. There is no database anywhere in the system.
keyResults: BYOK credential encrypted with AES-256-GCM using the user id as additional authenticated data, so a cookie lifted from one account and replayed into another fails the tag check and returns null

No database at all: sessions are JWTs, the provider key is an httpOnly cookie, the live exam is Zustand backed by sessionStorage, saved papers are localStorage, and rate-limit buckets are an in-memory Map. Five environment variables and nothing to provision

Counts Private Use Area glyphs to decide a page needs rasterising (a Symbol-typeface pi extracts as U+F070, an integral as U+F0F2) and names the nine specific code points in the prompt so the model reads the image instead
Quality gate beyond schema validation: isWeakQuestion rejects plausible-but-useless parses, the route demands 25 questions per subject with at most 2 weak, and saving refuses to persist fewer than 75

Seven of the ten commits are attempts to fit vision transcription of a 75-question paper inside Vercel's 60-second function ceiling, resolved by issuing three separate per-subject requests of about 55 seconds each
50 tracked files and about 4,000 lines of TypeScript across 10 commits
